subject: Maths
title: Multiplying vectors by a scalar
subtitle: Vectors · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can multiply a vector by a scalar and understand its geometric effect.

key_vocab.definition: Multiplying a vector by a scalar (number) multiplies each component by that number. This scales the vector: changing its magnitude but not its direction (unless negative).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can multiply a vector by a scalar and understand its geometric effect.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: scalar -- Multiplying a vector by a scalar (number) multiplies each component by that number. This scales the vector: changing its magnitude but not its direction (unless negative).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply each component by the scalar. Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other.
k(a, b) = (ka, kb)
Scales magnitude by |k|, reverses direction if k < 0

Key examples:
  ✓ 3(2, 4) = (6, 12)  (multiply each component by 3)
  ✓ -2(1, 3) = (-2, -6)  (negative scalar reverses direction)
  ✓ (4, 6) and (2, 3) are parallel  (one is 2 times the other)
  ✗ 3(2, 4) = (6, 4)  (must multiply both components)
  ✗ -1(3, 2) = (3, 2)  (should be (-3, -2))

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – positive scalar
  Calculate 4(2, 3).
  Multiply x: 4 × 2 = 8
  Multiply y: 4 × 3 = 12
  Result: (8, 12)
  (8, 12)
  (Each component is multiplied by the scalar.)

Example 2 – negative scalar
  Calculate -3(1, -2).
  Multiply x: -3 × 1 = -3
  Multiply y: -3 × (-2) = 6
  Result: (-3, 6)
  (-3, 6)
  (Negative scalar reverses direction.)

sections.title: Parallel vectors
sections.content:
State whether the vectors are parallel. If so, give the scalar.

(a) (4, 6) and (2, 3)
(b) (3, 5) and (6, 10)
(c) (1, 2) and (3, 5)
(d) (-4, 8) and (2, -4)

sections.title: Combined operations
sections.content:
Given a = (2, 3) and b = (4, -1), calculate:

(a) 3a
(b) a + 2b
(c) 3a - b
(d) 2a + 3b
(e) -a + 4b

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 3(2, 4) = (6, 12)
✗ 3(2, 4) = (6, 4)
✓ Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other
✗ -1(3, 2) = (3, 2)
✓ If a = 2b, then a and b are parallel and a is twice as long
